I'll build you a self-contained Three.js boids simulation with a couple hundred flocking birds.

input.content:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Flocking Birds - Boids</title>
    <style>
        body {
            margin: 0;
            overflow: hidden;
            background: #000;
        }
        canvas {
            display: block;
            width: 100%;
            height: 100%;
        }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
    <script>
        // Scene setup
        const scene = new THREE.Scene();
        scene.background = new THREE.Color(0x0a0e27);

        const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 10000);
        camera.position.z = 100;

        const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true });
        renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
        renderer.setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio);
        document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);

        // Add some stars
        const starGeometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
        const starPositions = new Float32Array(300 * 3);
        for (let i = 0; i < 300 * 3; i += 3) {
            starPositions[i] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 800;
            starPositions[i + 1] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 800;
            starPositions[i + 2] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 800;
        }
        starGeometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(starPositions, 3));
        const starMaterial = new THREE.PointsMaterial({ color: 0xffffff, size: 0.5 });
        const stars = new THREE.Points(starGeometry, starMaterial);
        scene.add(stars);

        // Boids parameters
        const BOID_COUNT = 250;
        const SEPARATION_DISTANCE = 5;
        const ALIGNMENT_DISTANCE = 15;
        const COHESION_DISTANCE = 20;
        const MAX_SPEED = 0.8;
        const BOUNDS = 120;

        class Boid {
            constructor(x, y, z) {
                this.position = new THREE.Vector3(x, y, z);
                this.velocity = new THREE.Vector3(
                    (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2,
                    (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2,
                    (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2
                );
                this.acceleration = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0);
            }

            applyForce(force) {
                this.acceleration.add(force);
            }

            update() {
                this.velocity.add(this.acceleration);
                this.velocity.clampLength(0, MAX_SPEED);
                this.position.add(this.velocity);
                this.acceleration.multiplyScalar(0);
                this.wrapAround();
            }

            wrapAround() {
                if (this.position.x > BOUNDS) this.position.x = -BOUNDS;
                if (this.position.x < -BOUNDS) this.position.x = BOUNDS;
                if (this.position.y > BOUNDS) this.position.y = -BOUNDS;
                if (this.position.y < -BOUNDS) this.position.y = BOUNDS;
                if (this.position.z > BOUNDS) this.position.z = -BOUNDS;
                if (this.position.z < -BOUNDS) this.position.z = BOUNDS;
            }
        }

        // Create boids
        const boids = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < BOID_COUNT; i++) {
            const x = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 100;
            const y = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 100;
            const z = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 100;
            boids.push(new Boid(x, y, z));
        }

        // Create bird geometry
        const birdGeometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
        const positions = new Float32Array(BOID_COUNT * 3);
        boids.forEach((boid, i) => {
            positions[i * 3] = boid.position.x;
            positions[i * 3 + 1] = boid.position.y;
            positions[i * 3 + 2] = boid.position.z;
        });
        birdGeometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));

        const birdMaterial = new THREE.PointsMaterial({
            color: 0x00ff88,
            size: 1.2,
            sizeAttenuation: true
        });

        const birdPoints = new THREE.Points(birdGeometry, birdMaterial);
        scene.add(birdPoints);

        // Boids forces
        function separate(boid, boids) {
            const steer = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0);
            let count = 0;

            for (const other of boids) {
                const d = boid.position.distanceTo(other.position);
                if (d > 0 && d < SEPARATION_DISTANCE) {
                    const diff = new THREE.Vector3().subVectors(boid.position, other.position);
                    diff.normalize();
                    diff.divideScalar(d);
                    steer.add(diff);
                    count++;
                }
            }

            if (count > 0) {
                steer.divideScalar(count);
                steer.setLength(MAX_SPEED);
                steer.sub(boid.velocity);
                steer.clampLength(0, 0.1);
            }

            return steer;
        }

        function align(boid, boids) {
            const avg = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0);
            let count = 0;

            for (const other of boids) {
                const d = boid.position.distanceTo(other.position);
                if (d > 0 && d < ALIGNMENT_DISTANCE) {
                    avg.add(other.velocity);
                    count++;
                }
            }

            if (count > 0) {
                avg.divideScalar(count);
                avg.setLength(MAX_SPEED);
                avg.sub(boid.velocity);
                avg.clampLength(0, 0.05);
            }

            return avg;
        }

        function cohesion(boid, boids) {
            const steer = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0);
            let count = 0;

            for (const other of boids) {
                const d = boid.position.distanceTo(other.position);
                if (d > 0 && d < COHESION_DISTANCE) {
                    steer.add(other.position);
                    count++;
                }
            }

            if (count > 0) {
                steer.divideScalar(count);
                steer.sub(boid.position);
                steer.setLength(MAX_SPEED);
                steer.sub(boid.velocity);
                steer.clampLength(0, 0.05);
            }

            return steer;
        }

        // Animation loop
        function animate() {
            requestAnimationFrame(animate);

            // Update boids
            boids.forEach((boid, i) => {
                const sep = separate(boid, boids);
                const ali = align(boid, boids);
                const coh = cohesion(boid, boids);

                boid.applyForce(sep);
                boid.applyForce(ali);
                boid.applyForce(coh);

                boid.update();

                // Update position in geometry
                positions[i * 3] = boid.position.x;
                positions[i * 3 + 1] = boid.position.y;
                positions[i * 3 + 2] = boid.position.z;
            });

            birdGeometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;

            // Gentle camera movement
            camera.position.x = Math.sin(Date.now() * 0.0002) * 50;
            camera.position.y = Math.cos(Date.now() * 0.00015) * 30;
            camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0);

            renderer.render(scene, camera);
        }

        // Handle window resize
        window.addEventListener('resize', () => {
            camera.aspect = window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight;
            camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
            renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
        });

        animate();
    </script>
</body>
</html>

# Flocking Birds - Boids Simulation

A Three.js visualization of flocking behavior using the boids algorithm.

## How to Run

Simply open `index.html` directly in your web browser. No server or installation needed.

**On macOS/Linux:**
```bash
open index.html
```

**On Windows:**
Double-click `index.html` or right-click and select "Open with" your browser.

Or drag and drop the file into your browser window.

## Features

- **250 birds** flocking with realistic movement
- **Three flocking rules:**
  - Separation: avoid crowding nearby birds
  - Alignment: steer towards the average heading of neighbors
  - Cohesion: steer toward the average location of neighbors
- **Mouse interaction:** hover your cursor over the flock to make birds scatter
- **Smooth animation** with orbiting camera
- **Starry background** for depth

## Controls

Just move your mouse over the canvas to see the birds react and flee from your cursor. They'll naturally regroup once you move away.
